problem: Find the equilibrium solutions of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡x+2.$

choices.value: The equation has no equilibrium solutions

feedback.problem: Find the equilibrium solutions of the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}={y}^{2}-6y+9.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given an autonomous differential equation ${y}^{′}(x)=f(y),$ if there exists a constant $c$ such that $f(c)=0,$ then $y=c$ is an equilibrium solution of the equation.

So, to find the equilibrium solutions of a differential equation, we must find all values of $c$ such that $f(c)=0.$

In our case, we have that $f(y)={y}^{2}-6y+9,$ so we attempt solve the equation $f(c)=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(c) & =0 \\ {c}^{2}-6c+9 & =0 \\ (c-3)^{2} & =0 \\ c-3 & =0 \\ c & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${y}_{1}(x)=3$  is the only equilibrium solution of the given differential equation.
